context: Parallel coordinates chart with 'strum brush' interaction for filtering 2000 synthetic alloy records across 8 dimensions, with linked scatter plots that appear when strums are drawn
first_impression: Structurally honest parcoords with data-driven scales and a colorblind-safe palette, let down slightly by index-based strum keys that can corrupt identity on mid-list removal.
what_works: Each axis uses `d3.extent(data, r => r[d]).nice()` — fully data-driven domains with no hardcoded magic numbers; scatter plot data joins use `d => d.id` key functions ensuring correct object constancy when the selected subset changes.
what_doesnt: Strum overlay data join keys off array index `(_, i) => i` rather than a stable strum ID, so removing a strum from the middle re-assigns indices and can misrender surviving strums; scatter panel key also mixes strum content with positional index (`${d.dimLeft}-${d.dimRight}-${i}`), creating the same fragility under permutation.
